findings.evidence: The proofs use only `asIso f`, `⟨X⟩` and `Iso.refl`. No such instances exist in `mathlib/Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Core.lean` (grep for Full/EssSurj/IsEquivalence/IsGroupoid finds nothing) or in `TauCeti/CategoryTheory/Core.lean`.
findings.fix: Move them to `TauCeti/CategoryTheory/Core.lean` with signature `{C : Type u} [Category C] [IsGroupoid C] : (Core.inclusion C).Full` (and likewise for the other two), and remove them from the monoidal file.
findings.issue: The instances `(inclusion C).Full`, `.EssSurj` and `.IsEquivalence` sit under the file-level `[MonoidalCategory C]` variable. That instance is auto-included because it depends only on `C`, so these facts require a monoidal structure they never use and don't apply to a plain groupoid.

findings.evidence: The `refine` proof uses only `toSkeleton_eq_toSkeleton_iff`, `congr_toSkeleton_of_iso (isoMk e)` and `fromSkeleton`. None of these involves the tensor structure.
findings.fix: Add `Core.skeletonEquiv {C} [Category C] : Skeleton (Core C) ≃ Skeleton C` (built from `(inclusion C).mapSkeleton` or from `toSkeleton`/`fromSkeleton`), then define `skeletonMulEquiv` as `{ skeletonEquiv with map_mul' := ... }` or via `.ofBijective` using `skeletonEquiv.bijective`.
findings.issue: The bijection `Skeleton (Core C) → Skeleton C` holds for any category: objects are isomorphic in `Core C` exactly when they are isomorphic in `C`. Here it is proved only inside `skeletonMulEquiv` under `[MonoidalCategory C]`.

summary: The monoidal, braided and symmetric structures are at the natural level, but the groupoid equivalence instances and the iso-class bijection carry a monoidal assumption they don't use. Both should be stated for any category and specialized afterwards.
